nodes.label: Adversarial Review Round 2
nodes.rationale: Five hostile reviewers were briefed to attack rather than encourage, because prior friendly persona critique had not surfaced viability, liability, or buildability failures; their findings became numbered decisions D1-D15 that the v3 mocks and BUILD-PLAN.md cite.

nodes.label: Reviewer: Bearish Seed Investor
nodes.rationale: Attacked viability, retention, incumbents, and the missing revenue line: Phase 1 ships vitamins and defers the painkiller, nobody opens the app in month 3, the Report screen is a strictly worse 311, and cold start is a map of gray rectangles.

nodes.label: Reviewer: Jaded Principal Designer
nodes.rationale: Attacked the gaps between screens and mock-versus-spec honesty: the mocks depict year three of a community that does not exist, the entire front door (permissions, sign-in, consent, decline paths) is missing, and sixteen required screens are unmocked.

nodes.label: Reviewer: Senior City Arborist
nodes.rationale: Attacked measurement validity, liability, privacy, and integration reality: the nightly export publishes unverified citizen observations as a citable dataset, wrong-tree attribution poisons timelines forever, and a hazard note is a discoverable liability record that auto-deletes.

nodes.label: Reviewer: Gamification Skeptic
nodes.rationale: Watched leaderboards poison three citizen science communities; argued every ranked metric is farmable in under thirty seconds and farmed check-ins are indistinguishable from honest ones in the database forever.

nodes.label: Reviewer: Staff Engineer (Buildability)
nodes.rationale: Told 'an LLM will build this from these documents' and attacked ambiguity: no API specification, no species content pipeline, nicknames only in mocks, ingest named but unspecified, and fifteen load-bearing ambiguities.

nodes.label: Goodhart's Law Applied to Tree Metrics
nodes.rationale: Burst photos pollute the timeline the future AI pipeline depends on; a countable check-in costs three seconds with every field skipped; 'watered' is a free unverifiable claim; favorites are sockpuppet-scalable. Extrinsic crowding-out drives away exactly the users Phase 1 lives on.
nodes.norm_label: goodhart's law applied to tree metrics

nodes.label: D1: The Leaderboard Dies
nodes.rationale: Screen 12 contradicted DESIGN.md's own 'no streaks or leaderboards' and screen 8's 'there are no leaderboards to game'; ranked raw counts with no verification machinery would have paid users to spam the record and poisoned the health time series at the source.

nodes.label: Neighborhood Almanac
nodes.rationale: Replaces the leaderboard: non-ranked, no counts attached to countable actions. First bloom sightings, oldest tree, species mix, coverage panel. Notices trees instead of scoring people.

nodes.label: Coverage Gaps as the Only Directed Incentive
nodes.rationale: Coverage is the one metric where chasing it produces exactly the data you want; ranked metrics route attention toward Grandmother Cypress and away from the young street trees in low-canopy neighborhoods that most need eyes.
nodes.norm_label: coverage gaps as the only directed incentive

nodes.label: D2: Honest Small Multiples
nodes.rationale: Unscaled small multiples let a 41-photo series and a 9-care series occupy identical heights; the three remaining charts share one scale and the favorites series is cut because favorites per month is nonsense for a one-time toggle.

nodes.label: D3: Anchored Vitality Rows
nodes.rationale: Five flat paint chips are indistinguishable in sun glare and for roughly 8 percent of male volunteers with color vision deficiency; full-width rows carry a reference photo, label, and always-visible anchor sentence, with color demoted to secondary coding.

nodes.label: D4: Hazard Reporting Is Redirect-Only
nodes.rationale: A public hazard community note is a discoverable liability record that then auto-deletes on a 90 day timer; what remains after the 311 handoff is a private reminder on your own record, never public, never auto-staled.

nodes.label: D5: Species-Aware Phenology Surfaces
nodes.rationale: The flagship Monterey Cypress, an evergreen conifer, showed 'Fall color starting!' in its timeline; the chip set is now driven by a leaf retention attribute on species so evergreens never show fall color.

nodes.label: D6: Tree ID Confirmation Step
nodes.rationale: Urban canyon GPS degrades to 20-50 m while street trees sit 6-10 m apart, so GPS-ranked ID with no confirmation and append-only records makes misattribution silent and permanent; per-contribution GPS accuracy is stored and low-accuracy contributions are excluded from growth charting.

nodes.label: D7: Minimal Measurement Capture in Phase 1
nodes.rationale: Growth history charted numbers no screen could enter; a measure sheet with keypad, mandatory unit and method chips gives screens 3 and 11 a legal data source. Estimated and taped points render as separate series and are never connected, because eyeball height carries roughly 30 percent error.
nodes.norm_label: d7: minimal measurement capture in phase 1

nodes.label: D8: Five Missing Screens Get Mocked
nodes.rationale: Cold tree profile, sign-in with license consent and decline path, measure sheet, outbox with retry, and post-check-in next-nearest flow. Only the five that change the product's shape were mocked: a mock set is an argument, not an inventory.
nodes.norm_label: d8: five missing screens get mocked

nodes.label: D9: Accounts Come Later in the Funnel
nodes.rationale: The signup wall landed on second 8 of a ten second visit, putting an auth sheet plus a license consent checkbox on the single conversion moment at a street corner; first saves are anonymous and local under a device ID, and the ask comes at the third save when the user has something to lose.
nodes.norm_label: d9: accounts come later in the funnel

nodes.label: D10: Phenology Notifications in Phase 1
nodes.rationale: They are the only mechanism that gives a tree a reason to summon a person back, and the species seasonal data they need is already in the schema; retention got a mechanism instead of a hope.

nodes.label: D11: Privacy Hardening
nodes.rationale: Public attributed visit timelines plus 'adopted by you' on a public surface reconstruct where a named person lives and stands, and volunteer programs include minors; feeds are private by default with opt-in attribution, adopter identity is never public, and an age gate lands in onboarding.

nodes.label: D12: Export Verification State Stamp
nodes.rationale: Provenance labels in the UI do not help a downstream script pulling the file; citizen observation rows carry a machine-readable unverified marker and the structured observation export holds until a verification tier ships.

nodes.label: D13: Phase Inversion Around the Org Wedge
nodes.rationale: The enthusiast layer needs thousands of users to feel alive; the steward loop works with ten. The org loop moves into a Phase 1.5 starting as soon as the walking skeleton stands, so the enthusiast layer launches into a map already carrying fresh steward data.
nodes.norm_label: d13: phase inversion around the org wedge

nodes.label: D14: Paid Org Coordinator Tier
nodes.rationale: The doc wrote a data escrow exit clause before a pricing page; org tooling is the paid tier at roughly 50-200 dollars per org per month, consumer free forever, and if no org will pay even that we want to learn it at design stage.

nodes.label: D15: BUILD-PLAN as Buildability Contract
nodes.rationale: The mocks and the spec described two different products with no API specification at all, so the mobile and web halves would have invented it differently; BUILD-PLAN.md must carry the field-level data model, API contract, ingest spec, sync design, privacy spec, milestones with acceptance criteria, and one-sentence ambiguity resolutions.

nodes.label: The Provenance Spine
nodes.source_location: What every reviewer said to keep
nodes.rationale: Method and unit metadata on every number, versioned species assertions, stable citable tree UUIDs, and lifecycle states survived five hostile reads untouched; the arborist called it genuinely rare.

nodes.label: Honest Routing
nodes.source_location: What every reviewer said to keep
nodes.rationale: 'The city has not been notified' as an explicit, mocked state with hazards hard-redirected to 311 was praised by all five reviewers as the most trustworthy decision in the design, which is why the Report screen survived the investor's demand to cut it.

nodes.label: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay
nodes.source_location: What every reviewer said to keep
nodes.rationale: The one artifact the official city app will never have: a longitudinal, framing-consistent visual record of individual trees. If the product pivots, it pivots around this.
nodes.norm_label: longitudinal photo timeline with ghost overlay
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: Cypress Build Plan
nodes.rationale: The document a future coding agent builds from; exists because an adversarial buildability review found DESIGN.md and SPEC-PHASE1.md left too much to invent. Precedence when documents disagree: BUILD-PLAN, then SPEC-PHASE1, then DESIGN.

nodes.label: Sequencing and the Wedge
nodes.rationale: Build order inverts the original phasing per D13: walking skeleton, Phase 1 core, Phase 1.5 org loop piloted with one partner org, then enthusiast polish.

nodes.label: Walking Skeleton (M0)
nodes.rationale: Real DataSF import end to end, clustered pins from tiles built by the pipeline, one visit round-tripping through the offline outbox and appearing on the public web tree page: proves every layer touches before features are added.

nodes.label: Stack Decisions
nodes.rationale: Expo/React Native + Next.js over Node 22/Fastify and Postgres 16 + PostGIS, decided rather than suggested, so an implementer does not substitute without a written reason.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: Self-Built PMTiles Map Pipeline
nodes.rationale: MapLibre GL on both clients over tippecanoe-built PMTiles regenerated nightly, with status and species baked into tiles so filters evaluate client-side: no Mapbox account, no per-seat licensing.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: Two-Phase Photo Upload Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Client gets a presigned PUT then references photo_id in the sync item; EXIF GPS and all EXIF metadata are stripped server-side, with capture timestamp and fuzzed coordinates stored in columns, never in the file. Orphan photo records are garbage-collected after 72 h.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: users table
nodes.rationale: Carries birth_year_bucket (no birthdates collected), public_attribution opt-in, and a versioned license_version so a license text change forces re-consent.

nodes.label: devices table
nodes.rationale: Anonymous contributions attach to device_uuid and migrate to the user on account creation, which is what makes the late account ask (D9) possible.

nodes.label: trees table
nodes.rationale: Holds external_ref to DataSF TreeID, site_lineage linking a replanted site to its predecessor, dbh_city_cm_range as a range because seed data is never a point, and verification_state per D12.

nodes.label: tree_names table
nodes.rationale: Nicknames existed only in the mocks with no field, no naming flow, and no moderation path; one active name per tree, first namer wins, renames go through the photo moderation queue, and the species common name is the fallback.

nodes.label: species table
nodes.rationale: leaf_retention drives phenology chips and season strip rendering (D5), and fall_color_months must be empty when leaf_retention is evergreen — enforced as a schema invariant test.

nodes.label: species_assertions table
nodes.rationale: Append-only with superseded_by self-reference so a reclassification keeps its history and its attributor, instead of a flat species foreign key that silently overwrites.

nodes.label: visits table
nodes.rationale: client_uuid is the idempotency key for outbox dedupe; gps_accuracy_m is captured per contribution per D6; phenology_tags validate against the species seasonal vocabulary.

nodes.label: photos table
nodes.rationale: shot_type and moderation_state gate what reaches public surfaces; blur_applied records that the face and license-plate detector ran at upload.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: observations table (check-ins)
nodes.rationale: structure_flags carry the UI label 'informal observations, not a risk assessment' into the export header so a downstream consumer cannot mistake them for a risk assessment.

nodes.label: measurements table
nodes.rationale: Stores value, unit_entered, canonical si_value, and method (tape, caliper, estimate, laser) plus measurement_height_m; estimated and measured points are separate chart series and points above 15 m GPS accuracy are excluded from per-tree charts.

nodes.label: care_events table
nodes.rationale: Actions are recorded but never publicly counted or ranked (D1), because a countable care claim is free and unverifiable.

nodes.label: favorites table
nodes.rationale: Uses deleted_at as a tombstone rather than a hard delete, because offline sync needs to replay an un-favorite as a toggle event.

nodes.label: private_reminders table
nodes.rationale: Replaces the public hazard note per D4: never public, never auto-staled, so no discoverable liability record exists and nothing silently disappears on a timer.

nodes.label: community_notes table
nodes.rationale: A check constraint rejects hazard categories at the database level so hazards can only ever be 311 redirects; the 90 day stale_at therefore applies to non-safety categories by construction.

nodes.label: review_flags table
nodes.rationale: An observation reporting appears_removed opens a flag instead of mutating trees.status, so two offline users flagging the same tree produce two flags on one thread rather than a write conflict.

nodes.label: notif_subscriptions table
nodes.rationale: Bloom and new-growth windows fired by a daily job reading species.seasonal — the D10 retention mechanism built on data already in the schema.

nodes.label: Client-Side Outbox (SQLite)
nodes.rationale: Exponential backoff 30s/2m/10m/1h then hourly, capped at 48 h before a visible failed state with a retry button; the wifi-only toggle applies to photo binaries only so metadata never waits on wifi.

nodes.label: verification_state
nodes.rationale: city_record, org_verified, or unverified as a queryable column rather than UI-only provenance, because a downstream script pulling the export file never sees a UI badge.

nodes.label: API Contract (/api/v1)
nodes.rationale: One JSON API with a fixed error envelope carrying a retryable boolean and cursor pagination, written because there was no API specification at all and the mobile and web halves would have invented it differently.

nodes.label: POST /sync batch endpoint
nodes.rationale: Takes an array of outbox items with client_uuids and returns per-item applied/duplicate/failed status; server-side dedupe on client_uuid makes retries idempotent, and contributions are append-only except favorite tombstones.

nodes.label: GET /trees?near= shortlist
nodes.rationale: The what-tree-is-this shortlist ordered by distance, each row carrying one id_tip as its distinguishing tell so the D6 confirmation step has something to show.

nodes.label: DataSF Ingest Spec
nodes.rationale: Column mapping, row rules for null coordinates and site placeholders, and weekly diff semantics; removed-from-source rows with community activity open a removed_but_active flag instead of deleting, and community contributions are never deleted by sync.

nodes.label: sf_species_map
nodes.rationale: A checked-in CSV for roughly 570 distinct qSpecies strings authored highest-frequency first; the import fails loudly if more than 2 percent of rows hit the unmapped stub path, so silent taxonomic rot is impossible.

nodes.label: Species Content Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Roughly 100 curated species covering 90 percent of SF street trees, versioned as YAML in the repo and loaded by migration rather than hand-edited in production; licensed reference photos double as cold-start hero fallbacks badged 'reference photo', and the long tail gets a generic silhouette because no botany may be fabricated.

nodes.label: Unmocked Required Screens and States
nodes.rationale: Permission asks and denials, empty states, sign-in decline, duplicate-proximity warning, leaf-off vitality suppression, and the You tab enumerated with their milestone, so an implementer never has to invent a state.

nodes.label: Privacy Spec
nodes.rationale: Photo locations snap to a universal 25 m grid because parcel proximity is unknowable at the precision that matters; tree pins stay exact since trees are public objects. Account deletion anonymizes rather than deletes, and no birthdate is ever collected.

nodes.label: Resolved Ambiguities A1-A10
nodes.rationale: One sentence per ambiguity so nobody re-litigates them in code review; includes the correction that the spec's clustering sentence was backwards (cluster at zoom 15 and below) and the A8 caretakers threshold that hides the count below three distinct contributors.

nodes.label: Milestones with Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: Written because the original milestones were grocery lists with no acceptance criteria and the word 'test' appeared nowhere; each accepts on an observable behavior such as an airplane-mode visit reaching the public web page or a steward finishing ten trees in under 25 minutes.

nodes.label: Test Plan
nodes.rationale: Pins the behaviors that would otherwise rot silently: golden-file ingest, outbox chaos, schema invariants (no evergreen with fall_color_months, no public query returning a hazard note), and an export contract diff that fails CI.

nodes.label: Golden-File Ingest Test
nodes.rationale: A 5,000-row fixture plus a mutated second snapshot covering adds, removals, species changes, and a removed_but_active case, asserting exact resulting table states so merge semantics cannot drift.

nodes.label: Outbox Chaos Test
nodes.rationale: Scripted network flaps during a 20-item sync asserting zero loss and zero duplicates, because losing a morning's field data once sends a volunteer back to paper permanently.

nodes.label: Who Pays: Org Coordinator Tier
nodes.rationale: Consumer layer free forever including the export; the pilot org's refusal to convert at even the low price point is a written finding that returns to this document before more org features are built.

nodes.label: What a Coding Agent Should Not Do
nodes.rationale: No invented botany, no streaks or ranks or public counts, no connected estimate-and-measured series, no 'sent to the city' copy without a real 311 ticket id, no birthdates or passwords or exact photo GPS, and a stop-and-ask for any screen not in the mocks.
nodes.norm_label: what a coding agent should not do

nodes.label: Cypress Standing Rules (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: Loaded for every session and subagent; every rule was paid for by a real failure whose receipts live in docs/investigations/repeat-failures-postmortem.md, and when a rule conflicts with convenience the rule wins.

nodes.label: False Green (Signature Failure Mode)
nodes.rationale: An exit code never proves a test run: nohup returns the shell's success, a killed build leaves a truncated log under a wrapper claiming success, and a trailing echo in an && chain lies. Only 'Test run with N tests passed' means anything for Swift Testing.

nodes.label: Never Trust an Unwatched Artifact
nodes.rationale: Check mtime, provenance, and content before reading a log, screenshot, or build as evidence; stale DerivedData, reused log paths, uncommitted assets, empty console captures, blank screenshots, and a location-declined simulator have each produced a false conclusion here.

nodes.label: Verify on the Merged Tree
nodes.rationale: A branch's green proves only the branch; a green re-run proves a failure was intermittent, never why it happened.

nodes.label: Simulator Assignment and Concurrency Cap
nodes.rationale: One simulator per agent with the owner's iPhone 16 kept free, three concurrent xcodebuilds machine-wide including orchestrator runs; SQLITE_IOERR_VNODE on the slowest test means contention, not your change.

nodes.label: Camera Grant and Known Hangs
nodes.rationale: The unit suite hangs forever on a simulator that never granted camera access, but re-granting on a timer kills the running app mid-test; #expect on two large Data values hangs in Swift Testing's diff, so reduce to a Bool first.

nodes.label: Errata and Ruling Numbering Discipline
nodes.rationale: Branches write unnumbered entries to docs/errata-pending or docs/rulings-pending and the orchestrator splices the real number at merge; a gap in the E/R sequence is a live branch's reservation and must never be filled.

nodes.label: Schema Versions Are Never Reserved or Skipped
nodes.rationale: The opposite of errata numbering: one migration author per round, named explicitly, and a task that turns out to need a migration must stop and report.
nodes.norm_label: schema versions are never reserved or skipped

nodes.label: Worktree Setup and Continuous Commit
nodes.rationale: setup_worktree.sh copies the git-ignored ~103 MB seed; without it 13 tests fail on seedURL → nil and the agent chases a defect it did not cause. Limit deaths take every agent at once, so a stall with uncommitted work is the only way work is lost.

nodes.label: Facts in Your Brief May Be Wrong
nodes.rationale: Agents have correctly refuted brief premises many times; verifying each premise against the code or seed, and refusing a false one, is doing the job right.
nodes.norm_label: facts in your brief may be wrong

nodes.label: Code Rules (tokens, layering, spellings)
nodes.rationale: Core is pure Foundation, Data imports no UI framework, Features may import anything; no raw hex, font sizes, or radii, no SF Symbols, American spellings, and a zero-warning line across app and test targets.

nodes.label: A Confident Comment Is Where Bugs Survive
nodes.rationale: Never assert an invariant in a comment you have not verified; cite errata by number, never by pending filename, because pending filenames are rewritten at merge.
nodes.norm_label: a confident comment is where bugs survive

nodes.label: Do Not Invent Botanical or Civic Content
nodes.rationale: DECISIONS constraint 15; a screen or state not in the mocks is a stop-and-ask under constraint 21.
nodes.norm_label: do not invent botanical or civic content

nodes.label: Persona Critiques of Design Plan v1
nodes.rationale: Four persona agents reviewed DESIGN.md v1 and their critiques are preserved verbatim; the refinements were folded into v2 rather than rewriting the source, so the reasoning behind each change stays auditable.
nodes.norm_label: persona critiques of design plan v1

nodes.label: Persona: The Tree Enthusiast
nodes.rationale: Core complaint: the check-in is a health-inspection form rather than a way of noticing a tree, the plan casts enthusiasts as free sensors, and species ID — the actual hook — is parked in Phase 3 even though seeded city data already answers it.

nodes.label: Persona: The Weekend Volunteer
nodes.rationale: Core complaint: no route, block, or workday concept; offline in Phase 2 makes Phase 1 unusable in the field because paper never fails to sync; and a six-step wizard times out a 20-tree morning.

nodes.label: Persona: The City Forestry Worker
nodes.rationale: Core complaint: a parallel triage queue duplicates Cityworks and goes unwatched, hazard reports sitting in an app create liability with no owner, and one-time seed import means the map rots into false work within six months.

nodes.label: Persona: The University Professor
nodes.rationale: Core complaint: an unanchored 1-5 vitality scale is subjective ordinal noise no volume rescues, a role badge is not a calibration record, and deferring license and export to Phase 3 builds a proprietary silo nobody will invest field-campaign effort into.

nodes.label: What Tree Is This? as a First-Class Flow
nodes.rationale: GPS plus seeded city data gets 90 percent of the way there with no AI at all, so the enthusiast hook does not need to wait for the last phase.
nodes.norm_label: what tree is this? as a first-class flow

nodes.label: Anchored Vitality Rubric Demand
nodes.rationale: A '3' from a weekend member and a '3' from a trained steward are not the same measurement; explicit anchors tied to USFS crown dieback classes with reference photos per class are what make ratings poolable across observers, cities, and years.

nodes.label: Observer Competency Model
nodes.rationale: Per-protocol training records earned through calibration tasks let researchers filter or weight by skill and detect drift; without it one untrained member's misread DBH propagates into the verified record with no way to quarantine it.

nodes.label: Per-Field Method and Unit Metadata
nodes.rationale: Accept rough estimates always, but record which one it was per field: a rough estimate labeled as such is useful, while one indistinguishable from a taped DBH poisons the whole column. Unit chaos is unrecoverable after the fact, so store canonical SI and capture the entered unit.

nodes.label: Mortality, Removal, and Replacement Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Survival analysis is the single most valuable output of a longitudinal urban-tree dataset and the v1 schema literally could not express the end state; the tree ID must persist through removal and replanting.

nodes.label: Multi-Stem DBH Convention
nodes.rationale: Multi-stem trees are ubiquitous in urban plantings; a single scalar DBH with no measurement height, fork rule, or lean adjustment silently corrupts basal-area and biomass math.

nodes.label: Species ID as Versioned Attributed Assertion
nodes.rationale: A flat pointer hides misidentification: no confidence, no identified_by or confirmed_by, no genus-only or unknown option, and no audit trail when a tree is reclassified. iNaturalist's research-grade consensus model is the reference to steal from.
nodes.norm_label: species id as versioned attributed assertion

nodes.label: 311 / Work-Order Integration as Primary Triage
nodes.rationale: Do not show 'routed to SF Public Works' without a contracted integration behind it: that is a misrepresentation the city's attorneys will notice, and a hazard sitting open for three weeks is a discoverable record showing nobody acted.

nodes.label: external_ref Round-Trip to City Inventory
nodes.rationale: Praised by both the city worker and the professor as the thing most civic tree apps skip; it is the only reason volunteer data could ever flow back into the system of record, so it belongs in the core model rather than bolted on.

nodes.label: Offline Queue as Table Stakes
nodes.rationale: Volunteers who lose a morning's data to a dead zone go back to paper and never return for Phase 2; for a mobile-as-field-tool positioning, offline is not a stewardship feature.

nodes.label: Org Assignments, Routes, and Workday Mode
nodes.rationale: Adoption is a personal self-selected list and that is not how org work happens; a lead assigns blocks, and ten volunteers on one block need live claimed/done status or two people enter tree 12 and nobody touches 15.
nodes.norm_label: org assignments, routes, and workday mode

nodes.label: Care Performed vs Condition Observed
nodes.rationale: The Observation model had nowhere to record care performed, only conditions observed; those are different things, the org lead needs both, and the care log is the highest-frequency event in the system and simpler to build.

nodes.label: Data Ownership, FOIA, and Exit Plan
nodes.rationale: Procurement and city IT security review ask on day one who owns the observation data, whether the city can produce Cypress records under FOIA, and what happens if the vendor folds — civic apps fold.
nodes.norm_label: data ownership, foia, and exit plan

nodes.label: Cypress Design Plan v3
nodes.rationale: The product document, revised twice: v2 after four persona critics, v3 after five hostile reviewers. BUILD-PLAN.md is now the implementation authority where documents disagree.

nodes.label: Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Appreciation first and data second; never block a submission but always record method; honest routing; decisions cheap now and ruinously expensive to retrofit go in Phase 1; design to a time budget (visit 10s, care log 30s, steward check-in 90s).

nodes.label: Users and Roles
nodes.rationale: Roles are per organization so a user can be a plain Member globally and a Steward within one nonprofit; the Org coordinator role was added in v2 because a volunteer's lead usually works at a nonprofit rather than the city and needs a lighter dashboard.

nodes.label: Two-Speed Contribution (Visit vs Check-In)
nodes.rationale: The ten-second Visit (photo plus optional note, no judgment) was split from the structured steward check-in because making someone grade a tree's health to say hello kills the lightest interaction after two uses.

nodes.label: Tree (data model sketch)
nodes.rationale: Immutable UUID persisting through death, removal, and replanting with site_lineage linking old to new; status enables survival analysis and provenance is displayed distinctly for community-added trees.

nodes.label: Observation (structured check-in)
nodes.rationale: Steward-oriented with a 90-second target; every quantitative field carries value, entered unit, canonical SI, method, and range validation, and the young-tree form surfaces hardware first because stake and tie condition are the whole check-in for a two-year-old street tree.

nodes.label: Photo (shot types and phenology tags)
nodes.rationale: Originals retained with consented EXIF as deliberate future AI substrate; prescribed shot types plus the ghost overlay keep framing consistent enough for growth and phenology work later.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: CareRequest and Routing States
nodes.rationale: Hazard and emergency types are not accepted in-app at all; the routing enum makes 'the city has NOT been notified' a first-class state, and same-tree same-type reports cluster so thirty storm reports become one ticket with every reporter notified.

nodes.label: Species as a Field Guide Entry
nodes.rationale: Promoted from a data-model footnote to a learning surface, because the words that describe why an enthusiast opens the app — learn, discover, seasons — barely appeared in v1.
nodes.norm_label: species as a field guide entry

nodes.label: Seed Then Sync City Data
nodes.rationale: A stale map is worse than an empty one because it generates false work: volunteers file check-ins on stumps. Removed trees become memorial records rather than 404s, and city/volunteer conflicts surface in a review queue instead of auto-resolving.

nodes.label: Data Governance and Licensing
nodes.rationale: Declared at launch rather than Phase 3: ODbL/CC-BY, stable citable UUIDs, a documented export schema, and an escrow exit plan, because export is the real adoption path for cities and researchers and dashboards are not.

nodes.label: Phase 1: The Living Map and the Ten-Second Visit
nodes.rationale: Success metric is weekly enthusiast return rate and zero field data loss, not observation counts, because if people love visiting trees the data follows.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: the living map and the ten-second visit

nodes.label: Phase 2: Stewardship and Organizations
nodes.rationale: Succeeds when a volunteer completes a 20-tree Saturday route entirely in-app and the org lead never asks for the spreadsheet again; verification scales through trust tiers and anomaly flags because there is no raw inbox anyone will read.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Intelligence and Openness
nodes.rationale: AI health flags and growth estimation wait for the standardized photo timeline to exist; gamification, if kept, is org-scoped crew totals gated behind verification and never individual volume streaks.

nodes.label: Platform and Architecture
nodes.rationale: Mobile is the field and walk tool, web is the depth tool, one account everywhere; Open311 GeoReport v2 is the standard care-request rail with per-city connectors only for onboarded departments.

nodes.label: Data Quality and Moderation
nodes.rationale: Per-field attribution becomes the substrate for competency-weighted trust rather than a lone verified flag; when data conflicts the most recent trusted value wins for display and the full history is always retained.

nodes.label: Remaining Open Questions
nodes.rationale: Which crown rubric exactly (needs an urban forestry advisor before Phase 1 data collection), Open311 coverage per city, how much field guide content can be licensed rather than authored, and whether fenced add-a-tree survives if verification slips.

nodes.label: Sharpened Value Proposition (v3)
nodes.rationale: The official city tree map will always win at being official, so Cypress commits to the personal and temporal layer instead of gesturing at civic reporting it cannot yet deliver.
nodes.community_name: Longitudinal Photo Timeline with Ghost Overlay

nodes.label: Cypress Phase 1 Specification
nodes.rationale: Deepens DESIGN.md v2 for Phase 1; explicitly design-stage, with no implementation decision final until build kickoff. Its goal is an SF resident learning what the tree outside their door is and returning weekly while every byte stays clean for stewards, cities, and researchers later.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Success Metrics
nodes.rationale: Week-4 retention at 25 percent or better, zero field data loss, 60 percent of visits with a photo, and 80 percent of what-tree-is-this sessions ending on a profile — retention and data integrity rather than observation volume.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Scope (In and Out)
nodes.rationale: Orgs, assignments, Open311 routing, dashboards, verification workflows, and anything AI are explicitly out; hazard reports are not accepted at all, so the Report entry point ends in either a 311 redirect or a note labeled 'the city has not been notified'.

nodes.label: User Stories U1-U10
nodes.rationale: Each story carries measurable acceptance criteria (map under 2 s, a visit in 10 seconds, care log in 30, an export keyed on UUID and external_ref with the license in the file header) so the E2E suite can be written per story.

nodes.label: Screen: Map Home
nodes.rationale: Pin color follows status, community trees get a dashed outline pin, and the primary FAB is 'What tree is this?' with visit and add behind a long press. The clustering sentence here is backwards and is corrected by ambiguity A1.

nodes.label: Screen: What Tree Is This?
nodes.rationale: Nearest-first list with confidence hinting that auto-highlights the top card only when it is within 3 m and the runner-up is 10 m or more away; explicit low-GPS and empty states because urban canyon accuracy degrades badly.

nodes.label: Screen: Tree Profile
nodes.rationale: Order matters: hero photo and season strip first, then identity and ID tips, with the stats row and provenance label below the fold — story before stats, per the enthusiast critique.

nodes.label: Screen: Visit Sheet
nodes.rationale: Camera opens immediately with the last full-tree photo at 30 percent opacity as a ghost overlay; offline submit always succeeds locally and shows a 'will sync' glyph so the user never waits on a spinner in the field.

nodes.label: Screen: Care Log
nodes.rationale: Chip toggles only, thirty seconds or less, because care performed is the highest-frequency field event and must never require the condition form.

nodes.label: Screen: Light Check-In
nodes.rationale: One scrollable card rather than a step wizard, because step-per-screen navigation with gloves in sun glare is death by transition animation; everything is skippable, only status defaults, and the target is 60 seconds.

nodes.label: Screen: Report (Community Note)
nodes.rationale: Hazard categories go to a full-screen tap-to-call 311; this spec still offers 'also pin a community note' on the hazard path, which decision D4 later removes as a liability record.

nodes.label: Screen: My Grove and Journal
nodes.rationale: Favorites grid, chronological photo diary with monthly headers, and a species collection ring — learning disguised as collecting, framed as memory rather than adopted-tree management.

nodes.label: Screen: Onboarding and Account
nodes.rationale: Location permission with purpose copy then straight to the map, with the account sheet at the first save action; decision D9 later pushes that ask to the third save because the first save lands eight seconds into a street-corner visit.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Postgres/PostGIS Schema Sketch
nodes.rationale: Every numeric inside observation jsonb carries {value, unit_entered, si_value, method}; species_assertions keep full ID history via superseded_by; sync_conflicts and review_flags exist so nothing auto-resolves silently.

nodes.label: Vitality Rubric v0
nodes.rationale: Five classes with plain-language dieback anchors and inline reference photos, a simplified derivative of USFS urban crown-condition classes with the mapping documented in the export schema; deciduous species are rated only in leaf-on season while structure flags stay year-round. Needs advisor sign-off before launch.

nodes.label: SF Data Seed and Recurring Sync
nodes.rationale: Roughly 190k DataSF rows seeded, then a weekly diff whose merge policy only marks a vanished city row removed when there has been no community activity in 30 days; otherwise it opens a removed_but_active conflict and the profile becomes a read-only memorial.
nodes.norm_label: sf data seed and recurring sync

nodes.label: Offline Outbox (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: Every mutation is written locally first with a client UUID and synced FIFO with backoff; append-only contributions mean there are no merge conflicts, and the outbox is visible in the UI so it never gets silently stuck.

nodes.label: Export and Licensing (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: ODbL for the database and CC-BY 4.0 for photos, declared before any data is collected because retroactive relicensing of contributed data is impossible; the schema is versioned with i-Tree-compatible naming where a mapping exists.

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirements
nodes.rationale: Map cold start under 2 s, WCAG AA with 44 pt targets and a high-contrast sun-readable map style, GPS reduced to roughly 25 m for public photos near residential parcels — a rule BUILD-PLAN later makes universal because parcel proximity is unknowable at that precision.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Milestones M0-M4
nodes.rationale: Foundations, Explore, Contribute, Belong, Trust; the launch bar is all five complete plus an advisor-approved rubric and a finalized license.

nodes.label: Species content sources, provenance and licence analysis
nodes.rationale: Written as the licence and provenance record backing the two species YAML files, and as the answer to PRODUCT.md open question 3 ('how much can be licensed/sourced openly versus authored'). Everything was fetched on 2026-07-21.
nodes.norm_label: species content sources, provenance and licence analysis
nodes.community_name: Cal Poly SelecTree (Urban Forest Ecosystems Institute)

nodes.label: Rule: do not invent botanical content
nodes.rationale: Every botanical value carries a citation to a source actually fetched during authoring, naming the field or quote it came from. Where no source could be found the value is null or an empty array. Nothing was written from recall and no citation was constructed to justify a value already written — the whole point is that a value and its evidence cannot drift apart.
nodes.norm_label: rule: do not invent botanical content
nodes.community_name: Cal Poly SelecTree (Urban Forest Ecosystems Institute)

nodes.label: Cal Poly SelecTree (Urban Forest Ecosystems Institute)

nodes.rationale: Primary source for leaf_retention (480 species directly, 19 more by genus uniformity) and the morphology facts behind id_tips. nodes.label: Quarantine of self-contradictory SelecTree records
nodes.rationale: Thirty-five records carry foliage_type = 'Evergreen' together with foliage_fall_color = 1. Sixteen are in the SF inventory (7,372 street trees), the largest being Prunus cerasifera at rank 6 with 6,670 trees, which is unambiguously deciduous. Taking SelecTree at face value would have written 'evergreen' onto the sixth most common street tree and, under D5, permanently suppressed its fall-colour chip. The pipeline quarantines the combination, falls back to NC State, and leaves leaf_retention null where no second source exists.

nodes.label: iNaturalist observation annotations (month-of-year histogram)
nodes.author: iNaturalist contributors
nodes.rationale: Source of bloom_months, fruit_months and fall_color_months. Places: San Francisco County (place_id=854) preferred, California (place_id=14) when the SF sample was too small, with the place actually used recorded in every citation. nodes.label: The one licence flag that matters: iNaturalist CC BY-NC
nodes.rationale: iNaturalist's default content licence is CC BY-NC and Cypress has a paid tier (D14). What was taken is month-of-year counts — facts about a dataset rather than the copyrighted observations — and the stored value is an array of integers. Defensible under US law (Feist: facts and non-creative compilations are not protected), but a position, not a permission. If iNaturalist has to be dropped the cost is bounded and known: eleven species lose bloom months, eight lose fruit months, Ginkgo loses the only fall_color_months in the repo; no leaf_retention, family, id_tips or care_notes value is affected.
nodes.norm_label: the one licence flag that matters: inaturalist cc by-nc

nodes.label: Seasonal month-array derivation rule
nodes.source_location: §7 'The derivation rule, stated so it can be checked'
nodes.rationale: Require at least 50 annotated observations (60 for fall_color_months); take the smallest run of consecutive months, wrapping the year boundary, holding at least 70 percent of them; emit only if that run is eight months or shorter, because a longer run means the annotation does not discriminate a season. Stated explicitly so it can be checked, and every citation records the taxon, place, observation count and full twelve monthly counts so the arrays can be recomputed or disputed without refetching.

nodes.label: API trap: verifiable=true silently zeroes annotated histograms
nodes.rationale: Combined with term_id, verifiable=true returns all-zero histograms for taxa that plainly have data — Ginkgo biloba coloured leaves in California returned 0 with the parameter and 408 without. The first full pipeline run included it. Do not send it.
nodes.norm_label: api trap: verifiable=true silently zeroes annotated histograms

nodes.label: API trap: iNaturalist taxa?q= returns confident wrong answers
nodes.rationale: Ficus nitida resolves to Ficus benjamina and Pyrus kawakamii to Pyrus calleryana var. calleryana. Both were caught only by reading the resolved names back, then overridden by hand, with the overrides recorded in the citations.
nodes.norm_label: api trap: inaturalist taxa?q= returns confident wrong answers

nodes.label: Metrosideros excelsa flowers in months 3-7 in San Francisco
nodes.rationale: The New Zealand Christmas tree flowers in December in New Zealand, but the San Francisco County histogram (n=102) puts its flowering in months 3 to 7. The northern-hemisphere shift is real and the data is right. This is the reason the arrays are taken from observations rather than from descriptions written for the plant's native range.

nodes.label: DataSF Street Tree List
nodes.author: City and County of San Francisco
nodes.rationale: Public open data, already the seed. Supplies the species strings and their frequencies. The qSpecies strings are messy — trade names, misspellings, superseded genera, cultivars and genus-only entries.

nodes.label: DataSF-to-source record matching ladder
nodes.rationale: Matching runs in a fixed order — selectree_name_exact (332), _species_level (52), selectree_synonym_other_taxa (50), gbif_backbone_species_key (21), selectree_primary_taxon (8), synonym species level (5), fuzzy edit distance 1 (5) and 2 (4), token subset (3) — and the method used is recorded in every leaf_retention citation so any single row can be audited. Fuzzy matching runs only after everything else fails, only for a single unambiguous candidate, only up to two edits, and all nine fuzzy matches were inspected by hand.

nodes.label: Genus-only strings get leaf_retention only under genus uniformity

Genera whose members disagree (Ulmus, Pyrus, Ficus, Ilex, Acer, Quercus, Prunus, Fraxinus, Magnolia, Salix) are left null rather than guessed.
